datasets.title: Geodata of Ajuong Thok Refugee Camp, Pariang County, Unity State, South Sudan
datasets.description: This map illustrates satellite-detected shelters and other buildings at Ajuong Thok refugee camp in Pariang County, Unity State, South Sudan. High resolution optical imagery collected by WorldView-1 show that as of 7 December 2013, a total of 2,997 shelters structures are present as well as 273 support structures within the 225 ha of the camp extent. Additional areas for camp expansion are well demarcated by the gridded network of dirt roads also visible. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR / UNOSAT.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/geodata-of-ajuong-thok-refugee-camp-pariang-county-unity-state-south-sudan-january-13-2014]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts reviewed high-resolution WorldView-1 optical satellite imagery from December 2013 to detect and map shelter and support structures within Ajuong Thok refugee camp. Building footprints were manually identified and classified by structure type, with confidence levels assigned based on image interpretation. The resulting spatial inventory provides a snapshot of camp infrastructure and expansion potential.
